source.title: Duality of Bures and Shape Distances with Implications for Comparing Neural Representations
source.authors: Sarah E. Harvey; Brett W. Larsen; Alex H. Williams

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper's numerical and analytical comparisons show that the choice of similarity measure can change reported similarity scores, refining the claim's metric-dependence version. It does not test convergence trends across trained models.
record.gate_note: The paper compares shape/Bures measures, NBS and CKA. Its relevant original results are the comparisons between NBS and CKA on generated PSD matrices and the stated analytic bounds; cited findings about neural models are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a theoretical paper on similarity measures. It proves that shape distance and NBS are dual, and shows that CKA and NBS can differ substantially. Its numerical comparison uses only Wishart-sampled random PSD matrices, not representations from trained models. It never measures how similar any two models are, so no convergence result bears on any version. The CKA-vs-NBS discrepancy is a general point about measures that is relevant to V6. It is not shown on model representations, so it goes under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors show that the Riemannian shape distance (cosine) equals NBS and that Procrustes distance equals Bures distance. This lets shape distances be defined between networks of unequal dimension and gives them clear asymptotic behaviour. CKA instead uses a Euclidean rather than Bures geometry on PSD matrices. Its relationship to NBS is bounded but loose, with scores differing two- to three-fold, so the two should not be expected to behave interchangeably. The authors explicitly say they are not arguing that Bures geometry is inherently superior.
record.recipe_differences: This is a theoretical analysis of similarity measures, with numerical comparisons on generated PSD matrices; it does not reproduce a model-convergence experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The similarity measure changes the reported scores: CKA and NBS can differ by two- to three-fold in the paper's numerical comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: On random Wishart PSD matrix pairs (10×10), CKA and NBS scores can differ two- to three-fold. They are related only within a loose envelope set by matrix rank (Eq. 24) and by Fuchs–van de Graaf-type bounds (Eq. 28).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different representational similarity measures (CKA vs NBS/shape distance) can give substantially different scores for the same pair of kernel matrices. Measure choice can therefore change reported similarity, though not yet shown on convergence across trained models.

record.problems: The numerical comparison uses generated PSD matrices rather than representations from trained neural networks. Figure values are not tabulated, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.

untested.parts: No trained models compared across scale or capability.
No networks trained from different seeds.
Proves that Procrustes distance equals Bures distance, a mathematical identity between measures. It does not test whether one model's representations can be mapped onto another's.
No convergence measurement on model representations under different measures, neighbour settings or inputs. The metric discrepancy is shown only on random PSD matrices and analytically.
No plateau, shared-data or shared-objective analysis.

missing.what: Rank-dependent envelope bounding squared NBS by CKA, saturated when both kernels have rank 1.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/'tests V6' with a 'supports' label is downgraded. The rows concern synthetic matrices and analytic bounds, not measured convergence between models, so no version-level verdict is given. The paper cites Li et al. 2015 (an original source) only in passing.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling or capability comparison of independently trained models.
No paired image-caption representations or cross-modal scaling comparison.
No networks trained from different initializations are compared.
The paper derives a relation between shape distance and Bures similarity, but does not test whether representations from different models can be mapped or stitched with little loss.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are tested.
Compares similarity measures on generated PSD matrices, not convergence measurements across neural models; does not vary neighbourhood settings or test different or out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of convergence plateaus, shared training data or shared objectives as explanations for alignment.

rows.subject: Wishart-sampled PSD matrix pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compared CKA and NBS for sampled PSD matrix pairs.
rows.measure: Difference between CKA and NBS similarity scores
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that CKA and NBS can differ by two- to three-fold.
rows.note: The plotted values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The subject is synthetic Wishart-sampled PSD matrices, not model representations, so the row does not measure convergence between models as V6 names. The 'two- to three-fold' figure is the paper's general statement about Fig. 2, not a value read for this sampling condition. There is no baseline.

rows.subject: Wishart-sampled PSD matrix pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compared CKA and NBS for a perturbed pair of PSD matrices.
rows.measure: Difference between CKA and NBS similarity scores
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that CKA and NBS can differ by two- to three-fold.
rows.note: The plotted values are not tabulated.
rows.check: The subject is synthetic perturbed PSD matrices, not model representations. As in R1, the value is the general text statement and is not specific to this condition. The row also overlooks Fig. 2(b), where the same samples are compared against the Eq. 28 bounds.

rows.subject: Centered PSD kernel-matrix pairs
rows.operation_detail: Compared NBS with CKA computed on the PSD square roots of the kernel matrices; derived bounds relating the scores.
rows.measure: Analytic bounds on the relationship between the similarity scores
rows.value: NBS(KX, KY) is bounded below by CKA(KX^(1/2), KY^(1/2)); Equation 28 gives further bounds. The lower bound in Equation 27 is saturated when KX and KY commute.
rows.note: The analytic result constrains the discrepancy; it does not establish equality in general.
rows.check: This is an analytic derivation (Eqs. 24, 27, 28), not an empirical measurement, so a 'partial' state does not apply. The rank-based envelope in Eq. 24 is omitted. NBS is bounded below by CKA of the square-root kernels, with equality when those matrices commute.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Generated PSD-matrix pairs and the paper's analytic comparison of NBS and CKA
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that CKA and NBS can differ substantially on the sampled pairs and derives bounds rather than an equivalence; this supports dependence on the similarity measure (R1–R3).
